newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end sharply lower on new crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end sharply lower on new crackdown.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices plunged on Thursday, triggered by Beijing's announcement of new crackdown measures on the stock market, brokers said.
The foreign currency B share index tumbled 13.63 points or 8.29 percent to close at 150.86 on turnover of HK$178 million compared with Wednesday's HK$49 million.
The domestic currency A index plunged 45.49 points or 9.73 percent to 422.14 on turnover of 8.3 billion yuan against 8.0 billion yuan the previous session.

Beijing on Wednesday announced it would ban state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading, in a move clearly aimed at curbing the inflow of "hot money" into the country's overheating stock market, brokers said.
"The intervention dealt a powerful blow to investor confidence and the shadow cast over the markets will not disappear soon," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
"The falls were a result of the ban, which will effectively weaken demand for equities," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

Numerous state and public firms have built heavy positions in the A share market and selling by these companies to comply with the new policy will continue to drag down the A index and could also hurt the B shares, analysts said.
"Further A share falls will, more or less, affect B shares," a trader said.
A market rebound is likely in the near future, but it is unlikely to be strong as sentiment has been dampened by Beijing's recent string of market-cooling moves, analysts said.

Beijing began to institute measures to cool down trading around the start of this month -- including announcing a huge quota of 30 billion yuan for new domestic share issues in 1997, doubling the 15 billion yuan quota for 1996.
The Shenzhen and Shanghai bourses have also recently imposed temporary suspensions on a number of A shares to allow investigations into alleged trading irregularities.
On the B share market, television tube maker Baoshi Electronics fell HK$0.35 to its 10 percent limit-down to end at HK$3.11.

Nanjing Posts & Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd, which listed 100 million B shares on Thursday, closed at HK$4.16 on its first day of trading, up 71 percent from the issue price of HK$2.43 per share.
Nanjing Posts opened at HK$3.98 and later hit an intraday high of HK$4.50 with 19.98 million shares changing hands during the day.
Brokers said Nanjing Posts was boosted by recent strong debuts posted by other B share firms, but was capped by overall poor market sentiment.
A number of A shares closed at their 10 percent limit-down, with household appliance maker Guangdong Macro sinking 0.60 yuan to 5.36 yuan.
